items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: John Malachi playing piano. Art Blakey at the drums.

ctx.x: Anyway, after Earl Hines' band, then Billy Eckstine formed a band, and he got all of the stars, you know. And he had -- at one time, he had -- let's see, in the reed section he had Dexter Gordon, Budd Johnson, Little Johnny Jackson -- I can't remember who the other one was. And in the trumpet section he had Dizzy, Fats Navarro, Shorty McConnell, and someone else I can't recall. I don't have total recall on the band. And he had two trombone players. One was Chippie Outcoul and another little trombone player out of…

did know his name. John Malachi playing piano. Art Blakey at the drums. And Tommy Potter playing bass. Well, Tommy got a case of pneumonia, so they called me out to substitute for him, and I had been laying off for awhile, you know, fingers were soft and everything, callouses were soft. And boy, it was a labor job the first night. So the next night I went prepared. I soaked my hands in powdered alum and hot water, as hot as I could stand it, you know, until they were water soaked, you know, like you see when…
Where was that? Was that here in Los Angeles?
